steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper that proposes GUI-based task-oriented dialogue and introduces the META-GUI dataset. It should cover the limits of API-based task-oriented dialogue systems, prior work on operating GUIs from language, what our task and dataset are, and our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Task-oriented dialogue systems and their pipeline
2. Drawbacks of API-based TODs
3. GUI as a more general interface; limits of prior GUI work
4. Proposed task (GUI-TOD) and the META-GUI dataset
5. Our agent and headline result
6. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Task-oriented dialogue systems
- rapid development in recent years
- applications: customer support, booking systems, especially intelligent personal assistants
- common pipeline: identify user intent -> slot-filling -> call backend APIs (from APP developers) -> response from query result

2. Drawbacks
- rely on publicly accessible APIs or APIs designed for TODs; such APIs may not exist in real-life APPs -> hinders application
- must be customized to recognize pre-defined API-related slots -> limits generality

3. GUI as interface
- humans on smartphones: no parametric API, just interact with the GUI (graphical user interface) -> GUI more general
- previous studies: translate natural language commands into GUI operations; but single query, step-by-step operations; real scenarios = multi-turn, no clear instruction on how to execute
- Etan, SUGILITE: learn GUI operations from demonstrations; script-based, sensitive to changes in GUI and workflow
- Duplex on the web: operates websites directly (e.g. booking a movie ticket); limited websites; more a unified GUI interface than a TOD with general GUI operation

4. GUI-TOD and META-GUI
- task: GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system (GUI-TOD); multi-turn conversation + direct GUI operation
- tasks performed on GUI of real APPs -> no TOD-specific APIs needed; TOD applicable on any APP
- no benchmark published -> collect META-GUI: dialogues + GUI traces on real Android APPs
- GUI trace = series of GUI operations: screenshots, Android view hierarchies, actions
- view hierarchy: XML-style file, hierarchical structure of GUI content; item types and bounding boxes (example in Appendix C)
- system opens related APP, executes task via multiple GUI operations; needs understanding of GUI structure and interaction logic (Figure 1)

5. Agent and result
- general ability to operate GUI, not optimized for specific APPs
- uses visual + textual information on screen; predicts next action, generates system response
- outperforms heuristic baselines by a large margin; action completion rate 82.74%

6. Contributions
- GUI-based TOD system performing tasks on mobile APPs through multiple GUI operations
- META-GUI dataset (dialogues + GUI operation traces) as benchmark
- thorough experiments; importance of multi-modal and history information; promising task, needs further exploration

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Task-oriented dialogue systems have developed rapidly in recent years. They are widely used for customer support, booking systems and especially intelligent personal assistants. These systems all work with a similar pipeline: first they identify the user intent, then they extract the necessary information with slot-filling. When the agent has enough information for the task, it calls the backend APIs (which are provided by APP developers) to get information, and then it generates a response based on the query result.

This framework has some drawbacks. First, TODs depend on APIs that are publicly accessible or designed for TODs to perform tasks, but such APIs may not exist in real-life APPs, and this hinders the application of TODs. Second, the system has to be customized to recognize the pre-defined API-related slots, which limits how general it is.

If we look at how humans perform tasks on smartphones, they don't need a parametric API, they just finish the tasks by interacting with the GUI (graphical user interface). This shows that the GUI is a more general interface. Previous studies explore how natural language commands can be translated into GUI operations. But these studies focus on a single query and step-by-step operations, while in real scenarios the query would be a multi-turn interaction and there is no clear instruction about how the task should be executed. Etan and SUGILITE are two systems that support learning GUI operations from demonstrations, but they are script-based and they are sensitive to changes in the GUI and the workflow. Duplex on the web can operate the website directly to do the required task, for example booking a movie ticket. But it only supports limited websites, and it is more a unified GUI interface than a task-oriented dialogue system that enables general GUI operation.

4. GUI-TOD and META-GUI
- task: GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system (GUI-TOD); multi-turn conversation + direct GUI operation
- tasks performed on GUI of real APPs -> no TOD-specific APIs needed; TOD applicable on any APP
- no benchmark published -> collect META-GUI: dialogues + GUI traces on real Android APPs
- GUI trace = series of GUI operations: screenshots, Android view hierarchies, actions
- view hierarchy: XML-style file, hierarchical structure of GUI content; item types and bounding boxes (example in Appendix C)
- system opens related APP, executes task via multiple GUI operations; needs understanding of GUI structure and interaction logic (Figure 1)

5. Agent and result
- general ability to operate GUI, not optimized for specific APPs
- uses visual + textual information on screen; predicts next action, generates system response
- outperforms heuristic baselines by a large margin; action completion rate 82.74%

6. Contributions
- GUI-based TOD system performing tasks on mobile APPs through multiple GUI operations
- META-GUI dataset (dialogues + GUI operation traces) as benchmark
- thorough experiments; importance of multi-modal and history information; promising task, needs further exploration

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Task-oriented dialogue systems have developed rapidly in recent years. They are widely used for customer support, booking systems and especially intelligent personal assistants. These systems all work with a similar pipeline: first they identify the user intent, then they extract the necessary information with slot-filling. When the agent has enough information for the task, it calls the backend APIs (which are provided by APP developers) to get information, and then it generates a response based on the query result.

This framework has some drawbacks. First, TODs depend on APIs that are publicly accessible or designed for TODs to perform tasks, but such APIs may not exist in real-life APPs, and this hinders the application of TODs. Second, the system has to be customized to recognize the pre-defined API-related slots, which limits how general it is.

If we look at how humans perform tasks on smartphones, they don't need a parametric API, they just finish the tasks by interacting with the GUI (graphical user interface). This shows that the GUI is a more general interface. Previous studies explore how natural language commands can be translated into GUI operations. But these studies focus on a single query and step-by-step operations, while in real scenarios the query would be a multi-turn interaction and there is no clear instruction about how the task should be executed. Etan and SUGILITE are two systems that support learning GUI operations from demonstrations, but they are script-based and they are sensitive to changes in the GUI and the workflow. Duplex on the web can operate the website directly to do the required task, for example booking a movie ticket. But it only supports limited websites, and it is more a unified GUI interface than a task-oriented dialogue system that enables general GUI operation.

So we propose the task of GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system (GUI-TOD). It supports multi-turn conversation and direct GUI operation. All the tasks are performed on the GUI of real APPs, so we don't need TOD-specific APIs to communicate with APPs anymore, and TOD could be applied on any APP. There is no available benchmark published, so we collect META-GUI, a dataset with dialogues and GUI traces on real Android APPs. A GUI trace is a series of GUI operations, which includes screenshots, Android view hierarchies and actions. The Android view hierarchy is an XML-style file that organizes the content of the GUI in a hierarchical structure. It also has the types of the items on the screen and their bounding boxes. An example is in Appendix C. When the user requests a task, the system should open the related APP and execute the task with multiple operations on the GUI. This needs a comprehensive understanding of the GUI structure and the interaction logic. Figure 1 shows an interaction example.

We focus on building an agent that has a general ability to operate GUI, not on optimizing for specific APPs. Our GUI-TOD system uses both the visual information and the textual information on the screen to predict the next action to execute and to generate the system response. In our experiments the GUI-TOD outperforms heuristic baselines by a large margin, with an action completion rate of 82.74%.

Our contributions are:

- We propose a GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system that can do tasks on mobile APPs with multiple operations on the GUI.

- We collect META-GUI, a dataset with dialogues and GUI operation traces, which is the benchmark for the proposed system.

- We do thorough experiments on our dataset and validate that multi-modal information and history information are important. We show that the task is promising but needs more exploration.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Recent years have seen the rapid development of task-oriented dialogue systems [1,2,3,4]. They have been widely applied to customer support, booking systems and especially intelligent personal assistants. These task-oriented dialogue systems work in a similar pipeline: first they identify the user intent, then they extract the necessary information through slot-filling. After getting enough information for the task, the agent calls the backend APIs (provided by APP developers) to fetch information, and then generates a response based on the query result.

This framework has some drawbacks. Firstly, TODs rely on publicly accessible APIs or APIs designed for TODs to perform tasks, but such APIs may not exist in real-life APPs, which hinders the application of TODs. Secondly, a system has to be customized to recognize the pre-defined API-related slots, which limits its generality.

Consider how humans perform tasks on smartphones: they don't need a parametric API but finish tasks by interacting with the GUI (graphical user interface), which indicates that the GUI is a more general interface. Previous studies explore how to translate natural language commands into GUI operations [5,6,7]. These studies focus on a single query and step-by-step operations, while in real scenarios the query would be a multi-turn interaction and there is no clear instruction about how to execute the task. Etan [8] and SUGILITE [9] are two systems that support learning GUI operations from demonstrations, but they are script-based and sensitive to changes in the GUI and workflow. Duplex on the web [10] can directly operate the website to perform the required task, for example booking a movie ticket. However, it only supports limited websites, and it is more a unified GUI interface than a task-oriented dialogue system that enables general GUI operation.

To this end, we propose the task of GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system (GUI-TOD). It supports multi-turn conversation and direct GUI operation. All tasks are performed on the GUI of real APPs, which means we no longer need TOD-specific APIs to communicate with APPs, and it becomes possible to apply TOD on any APP. Since no benchmark has been published, we collect META-GUI, a dataset with dialogues and GUI traces on real Android APPs. A GUI trace is a series of GUI operations, including screenshots, Android view hierarchies as well as actions. The Android view hierarchy is an XML-style file which organizes the content of the GUI through a hierarchical structure. It also contains the types of the items on the screen and their bounding boxes. An example is shown in Appendix C. When a user requests a task, the system should open the related APP and execute the task through multiple operations on the GUI. This requires a comprehensive understanding of GUI structure and interaction logic. An interaction example is shown in Figure 1.

We focus on building an agent with a general ability to operate GUI, rather than optimizing for specific APPs. Our proposed GUI-TOD system leverages both the visual and the textual information on the screen to predict the next action to be executed and to generate the system response. Our experiments show that GUI-TOD outperforms heuristic baselines by a large margin, with an action completion rate of 82.74%.

Our contributions are as follows:

- • We propose a GUI-based task-oriented dialogue system, which can perform tasks on mobile APPs through multiple operations on the GUI.

- • We collect META-GUI, a dataset with dialogues and GUI operation traces that serves as the benchmark for the proposed system.

- • We conduct thorough experiments on our dataset and validate the importance of multi-modal information and history information. We show that this is a promising task that needs further exploration.
